description.extended:
Baron by Richard Kern is the seventh issue of the London imprint's single-artist series, given over to Doubles, Kern's portraits of young women in which a clothed and a topless exposure of the same sitter are printed one over the other.

Published by Baron in 2021 in an edition of 1,000, the book runs to 128 pages in a large-format softcover, with art direction by Sam Boxer. The series began with a 1997 picture of a model in her school uniform and retainer. Around 2010 Kern started shooting each sitter both dressed and undressed, and in 2011 a zine printer's accidental overlay of the two frames on one page gave him the finished form. The sitters approach Kern themselves and pose without direction. The superimposition leaves the body half veiled, and Baron's text frames the pictures as a study of the passage from girlhood to womanhood rather than of nudity itself.

Kern (born 1954) came out of New York's No Wave scene and the Cinema of Transgression films of the 1980s, working with Lydia Lunch, Sonic Youth and Henry Rollins before turning to photography. New York Girls (1997) and Medicated (2020) are the nearest precedents for this book. The library also holds Baron's single-artist volumes with Harley Weir, Joyce Lee and Bruce LaBruce.
description.artist_bio: Richard Kern (born 1954) is a New York photographer and filmmaker who emerged from the No Wave scene and the Cinema of Transgression of the 1980s, collaborating with Lydia Lunch, Sonic Youth and Henry Rollins. His books include New York Girls (1997), Shot by Kern and Medicated (2020).

notes: Shelf: Araki / Kern. Baron Issue 7, the series titled Doubles; edition of 1,000, art direction by Sam Boxer, first edition 2021. Titled Baron to match Baron by Joyce Lee (id 2207); retailers list it as Baron by Richard Kern. A special edition with a print was also sold; the library copy is assumed to be the standard edition.
